keyVerseText: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:
rootMeaning: The Greek noun μέρος (méros) originates from an obsolete but more primary form of the verb μείρομαι (meíromai), which means 'to get as a section or allotment.' This etymology highlights the fundamental idea of a portion or share that is assigned or received, emphasizing division and distribution. Unlike the general English word 'part,' μέρος carries the nuance of something apportioned or allotted, whether literally or figuratively, which enriches its use in Scripture.
usageInScripture: With 43 occurrences, μέρος is predominantly translated as 'part' or 'parts,' appearing 18 times in these forms, but also as 'portion,' 'behalf,' and 'respect.' Its usage spans from describing physical divisions, such as regions or coasts, to more abstract concepts like a share in work, destiny, or duty. This broad semantic range shows that μέρος consistently conveys the idea of a distinct section or share within a whole, whether spatial, temporal, or relational.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding μέρος as an allotted share or portion enriches our grasp of biblical teaching on God's sovereign distribution and order. It reminds believers that every individual and event has a divinely appointed place and role within God's providential plan. The word's emphasis on division and assignment underscores the biblical truth that nothing is random; each 'part' contributes to the whole of God's redemptive work. This insight encourages trust in God's governance and invites believers to embrace their unique 'portion' in His kingdom, serving faithfully in the role allotted to them.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 2:22, the word μέρος appears in the phrase 'he turned aside into the parts of Galilee,' referring to specific regions or divisions of the land. Here, μέρος highlights the geographical and political subdivisions relevant to Joseph's protective move for Jesus. This usage reinforces the idea that God's guidance operates within real, distinct portions of the world, assuring believers that His care extends to every 'part' of their lives and circumstances.
